simple.meaning: שָׁקַק (shâqaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to course (like a beast of prey); by implication, to seek greedily.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, Joel, Nahum, beginning at Psalms 107:9. The surrounding contexts include city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁקַק (H8264) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׁקַק (shâqaq) / H8264 is traced through Psalms 107:9, Proverbs 28:15, Isaiah 29:8, Isaiah 33:4 with source-language evidence and verse context.

structuredEvidence.definition: to course (like a beast of prey); by implication, to seek greedily

firstOccurrence.englishText: For he satisfies the longing soul.

timeline.evidenceText: For he satisfies the longing soul.
As a roaring lion or a charging bear,

It will be like when a hungry man dreams, and behold, he eats; but he awakes, and his hunger isn’t satisfied; or like when a thirsty man dreams, and behold, he drinks; but he awakes, and behold, he is faint, and he is still thirsty. The multitude of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion will be like that.
Your plunder will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers.
He summons his picked troops. They stumble on their way. They dash to its wall, and the protective shield is put in place.

Hithpalpel Imperfect 3masculine plural יִשְׁתַּקְשְׁקוּן Nahum 2:5 , of chariots, they rush to and fro.
